headline: The Inc ransomware crew is chaining two SonicWall SMA zero-days into root-level control of remote-access appliances, as fresh disclosures show governments and criminals racing to hoard and exploit personal data.

emerging_trends.text: Ransomware crews keep turning enterprise remote-access hardware into their front door, with the Inc gang weaponizing SonicWall SMA zero-days for root-level control.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Inc Ransomware Chains SonicWall SMA Zero-Days to Root

emerging_trends.text: Bulk personal data now fuels both state surveillance and street-level fraud, as ICE commits $125 million to Thomson Reuters records while carders assemble clean proxies and stolen fingerprints.
emerging_trends.topic_title: ICE Buys Thomson Reuters Data to Hunt Voter Fraud

emerging_trends.text: Foreign intelligence services fixate on physical tracking, from Iran geolocating US military phones to Russian cyberspies pivoting into infrastructure hacking.

topics.title: Inc Ransomware Chains SonicWall SMA Zero-Days to Root
topics.latest_developments: Dark Reading laid out how the Inc ransomware crew chains two SonicWall Secure Mobile Access flaws in sequence to seize root-level control of the appliances.
topics.summary: SonicWall's Secure Mobile Access appliances sit at the network edge to broker remote-worker connections. Inc, a ransomware-as-a-service operation, exploits a pair of zero-days together to run commands as root; SonicWall customers should apply the vendor's fixes and hunt their appliances for signs of compromise.

sources.title: Inc Ransomware Exploits SonicWall SMA Zero-Days

topics.title: ICE Buys Thomson Reuters Data to Hunt Voter Fraud
topics.latest_developments: A procurement record shows US Immigration and Customs Enforcement will pay Thomson Reuters $125 million for access to names, Social Security numbers, and ethnicity data to investigate what it calls 'voters fraud' and immigration fraud.
topics.summary: ICE is buying bulk personal records from Thomson Reuters to mine for alleged voter and immigration fraud. The deal folds Americans' Social Security numbers and ethnicity into an immigration-enforcement dataset, drawing sharp privacy and civil-liberties objections.

sources.title: ICE to Pay Thomson Reuters $125 Million to Find 'Voter Fraud'

topics.title: Fairlife Halts US Dairy Production After Ransomware
topics.latest_developments: Fairlife named the plants the ransomware attack idled, sites in Michigan, New York, and Arizona, mapping the footprint of its suspended US production.
topics.summary: Fairlife, a Coca-Cola dairy subsidiary whose retail sales passed $1 billion in 2022, stopped US production after a ransomware attack. The disruption spans its plants in Michigan, New York, and Arizona.

sources.title: Dairy company Fairlife suspends production in US after cyber incident

topics.title: Carders Hunt Clean Residential Proxies
topics.latest_developments: Flare documented carders shifting to 'clean' residential proxies paired with browser fingerprints and device profiles to slip past modern fraud detection.
topics.summary: Residential proxies route criminal traffic through real home IP addresses to mimic legitimate shoppers. As fraud engines flag dirty proxies, carders now chase unflagged 'clean' ones and layer them with stolen device fingerprints and identity signals to cash out stolen cards.

sources.title: Inside the Search for "Clean" Residential Proxies for Carding

topics.title: Iran Tracks US Military Phones
topics.latest_developments: SecurityWeek reported that Iran is geolocating the mobile phones of US military personnel.
topics.summary: Iranian operators are tracking the physical locations of US service members through their mobile phones as an intelligence effort against American forces. Personnel should tighten location-sharing and harden device settings.

sources.title: In Other News: Iran Tracks US Military Phones, CrashStealer macOS Malware, CVD Blueprint

business_politics.title: Iran Strikes Saudi Arabia as Gulf War Widens
business_politics.latest_developments: Iran struck Saudi Arabia directly for the first time in months on Saturday, July 18, opening a front beyond the Kuwaiti desalination plant and Gulf shipping already reported.
business_politics.summary: The United States and Iran traded strikes on infrastructure and military targets across the Persian Gulf on Saturday, July 18, with Iran hitting Saudi Arabia as both sides pressed their fight over the Strait of Hormuz, raising the risk that the war spirals into a broader regional conflict that could choke oil and shipping.

sources.title: Iran strikes Saudi Arabia for first time in months
The U.S. and Iran Creep Toward a Wider War With Escalating Attacks

business.title: Westmoreland Lamb Demand Climbs as Wool Prices Fall
business.latest_developments: TribLive reported July 18 that growing Middle Eastern and Mexican populations are lifting demand for Westmoreland County lamb and mutton even as wool prices plunge.
business.summary: Sheep and lamb growers in Westmoreland County are selling more meat as the region's Middle Eastern and Mexican communities expand, though a collapse in wool prices squeezes the same producers who raise the animals.

sources.title: Westmoreland sheep, lamb market thrives on rising ethnic demand but wool prices plunge

business.title: Indiana Township Pizza Shop Rises From a Career Pivot
business.latest_developments: TribLive profiled July 18 how John English turned an unexpected career change into a fixture independent pizza shop in Indiana Township.
business.summary: John English never planned to sell pizza, and his unplanned career pivot into the trade has made his independent shop a food fixture in Indiana Township, Allegheny County.

sources.title: A slice of nice: Friendly independent pizza shop a food fixture Indiana Township

around_town.title: Smoke Clears Saturday as Severe Storms Move In
around_town.latest_developments: Air-quality alerts across the Pittsburgh region end just before 10 a.m. Saturday, July 18, as a wind shift clears the wildfire smoke, and forecasters now warn of severe storms with damaging winds, hail, and possible tornadoes after 3 p.m.
around_town.summary: The Canadian wildfire smoke that drove Pittsburgh's air into hazardous ranges this week lifts Saturday, July 18, as winds push it out. Forecasters made the day a Severe Weather Alert Day, with a line of strong storms threatening damaging winds, hail, and tornadoes across Western Pennsylvania from mid-afternoon into the evening; the poor air had already forced cancellation of Friday's America's Mile race.

sources.title: Air quality improves on Saturday in Pittsburgh, but strong storms possible throughout the day
Strong to severe storms Saturday in Western Pennsylvania
America's Mile race canceled because of poor air quality in Pittsburgh

around_town.title: Pittsburgh Skirts Its Own Police Residency Rule
around_town.latest_developments: TribLive reported July 18 that the city promoted a South Fayette resident to assistant police chief last month, despite rules that appear to require commanders to live in Pittsburgh.
around_town.summary: The Pittsburgh Bureau of Police promoted a South Fayette resident to assistant chief in June, a move TribLive found conflicts with a city residency rule that appears to require police commanders to live within Pittsburgh.

sources.title: Pittsburgh ignores its own residency rule for police commanders

around_town.title: Transit Chief Urges Drivers to Skip Parkway East
around_town.latest_developments: TribLive detailed July 18 how commuters are turning to buses and rail during the Parkway East closure, with Pittsburgh Regional Transit chief executive Katharine Kelleman telling drivers, "Don't drive."
around_town.summary: With the Parkway East (I-376) closed and roughly 100,000 daily drivers rerouting, Pittsburgh Regional Transit chief executive Katharine Kelleman is pressing commuters to leave their cars and ride the agency's buses and rail through the shutdown.

sources.title: Offbeat Pittsburgh: Surviving the Parkway East closure with public transit

events.title: Picklesburgh Extends Sunday Hours Downtown
events.latest_developments: The Pittsburgh Downtown Partnership extended Picklesburgh's Sunday hours, WPXI reported July 18, to help vendors recover after wildfire smoke thinned Friday and Saturday crowds.
events.summary: Picklesburgh, the Pittsburgh Downtown Partnership's food festival in Downtown Pittsburgh, closes Sunday, July 19, and partnership president and chief executive Jeremy Waldrup lengthened the festival's final-day hours to give vendors a stronger finish after wildfire smoke cut into attendance earlier in the weekend.

sources.title: Picklesburgh extends Sunday hours, hoping to help vendors finish 'unprecedented weekend' strong

around_teams.title: Curiel's Win-First Makeup Draws Pirates Praise
around_teams.latest_developments: A Post-Gazette profile July 18 detailed how first-round pick Derek Curiel, the LSU and Orange Lutheran outfielder, "does whatever it takes to win."
around_teams.summary: The Post-Gazette profiled Derek Curiel, the outfielder out of LSU and Orange Lutheran High School whom the Pirates took fifth overall in the 2026 draft, casting his win-at-all-costs makeup as the trait that drew the organization to him.

sources.title: There's 'no doubt about it': Pirates first-round draft pick Derek Curiel does whatever it takes to win

around_teams.title: Smoke Postpones Pirates-Guardians Opener
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported July 17 that the Pirates postponed their series opener against the Cleveland Guardians because of the hazardous air quality from Canadian wildfire smoke.
around_teams.summary: The Pirates called off their series opener against the Cleveland Guardians as wildfire smoke pushed Pittsburgh's air quality into unhealthy ranges, one of several regional events disrupted by the haze.

sources.title: Pirates' series opener against the Guardians postponed due to air quality conditions

team_usa.title: IOC Complaint Over Balogun Affair Likely to Fizzle
team_usa.latest_developments: The Guardian reported July 18 that FIFA president Gianni Infantino will probably escape IOC sanction over a human-rights group's complaint about his Trump dealings surrounding United States forward Folarin Balogun.
team_usa.summary: The human-rights organization FairSquare asked the International Olympic Committee to punish FIFA president Gianni Infantino after President Trump said he had phoned Infantino over the affair around United States forward Folarin Balogun's red card and lifted ban; the Guardian reported Infantino is poised to avoid any penalty.

sources.title: Gianni Infantino unlikely to face IOC sanctions over Balogun red card scandal
